briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's 24% Squeeze Deepens as Washington Fast-Tracks Schedule III and Curaleaf Goes Hostile on Aurora
briefs.top: Michigan's wholesale tax fight is now a full-blown election issue as closures pile up in the U.P. and Lansing, while in D.C. the DEA's rescheduling machine keeps grinding forward and Curaleaf turns up the heat on its Aurora takeover bid. Psychedelics are having a parallel moment, with Compass Pathways' psilocybin program picking up FDA fast-track status.

local.text: MiCIA's second lawsuit—joined by grower Mitten Distro X LLC and retailer Refine Michigan Co.—argues the 24% wholesale tax operates like a sales tax and creates unconstitutional "tax pyramiding," while a separate constitutional challenge over the same law is already headed toward trial.

Michigan's 2025 cannabis revenue fell roughly $113 million to $3.17 billion even as growers produced nearly 260,000 more pounds of flower, a margin collapse MiCIA director Robin Schneider has called devastating for operators.

Upper Peninsula chain Higher Love shut its Crystal Falls, Escanaba, Houghton, Munising and Ontonagon dispensaries this month, pointing to "the mounting tax burden on Michigan's adult-use cannabis industry" as it consolidates to four remaining stores.

The Michigan Supreme Court reset enforcement ground rules this summer, ruling in People v. Hess that MRTMA-compliant marijuana use can't be barred as a probation condition just because it violates federal law, a companion decision to its ruling curbing vehicle searches based on marijuana odor alone.

With Whitmer term-limited, GOP gubernatorial nominee John James used his "Freedom Agenda" rollout to vow repealing or rolling back the wholesale tax, saying it "drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections," while also pledging a crackdown on unregulated hemp THC products.

national.text: The DEA's marijuana-to-Schedule-III rulemaking cleared "a critical procedural checkpoint on August 18, 2026," a step that would eliminate 280E tax penalties—cutting effective operator tax rates from roughly 60% to the mid-20s—while leaving federal prohibition and interstate commerce largely intact.

Final briefs are now in from the DEA's cannabis rescheduling hearing, with the agency arguing opponents' case against Schedule III has "no merit" and pointing to an HHS report finding marijuana has a currently accepted medical use.

The federal intoxicating-hemp ban is still on track for Nov. 12 despite industry pressure: the Senate passed a 30-day delay via stopgap funding on Aug. 8, but the House doesn't return until Aug. 31, and until it acts, the original deadline stands.

Curaleaf escalated its $272 million hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis this week, accusing the company of "hollow protests and completely misleading statistics" after Aurora pushed back on Curaleaf's account of stalled merger talks.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin candidate COMP360 landed an FDA National Priority Voucher promising a 1-2 month NDA review, part of a rolling-submission push toward a possible first-half-2027 launch that also hinges on a White House-directed DEA review of psychedelic rescheduling.
